newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court annuls Commission communication on pension funds.
newsitem.headline: Court annuls Commission communication on pension funds.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Friday the European Commission acted outside the scope of its authority when it adopted and published a communication creating an internal market for pension funds.

The Council of Ministers of the European Union had failed to adopt a directive on the freedom of management and investment of pension funds with terms almost identical to the Commission's communication, three years earlier.
France brought the issue to the court, supported by Spain, and successfully argued the Commission's published communication created new legal effects for member states.

The court annulled the Commission communication on an internal market for pension funds, finding the Commission was "not empowered to adopt an act" which "intended to have legal effects of its own, distinct from those already provided for by the treaty."

Betty Olivi, the spokeswoman for Commissioner Mario Monti, said the Commission was unhappy with the decision, but noted the court did not rule against a single market in the pension fund area, only against the procedure the Commission used.

Olivi said the Commission is currently working on a green paper expected in May. "The Commission hopes to develop and refine issues which were included in the Communication, and would consider Community and member state interests in investment returns and pension fund management," Olivi said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
application for annulment of Commission Communication 94/C 360/08 on an internal market for pension funds (OJ 1994 C 360, p. 7)
1. Annuls Commission Communication 94/C 360/08 on an internal market for pension funds
2. Orders the Commission to pay the costs.
